verdicts.reason: Quotes verify verbatim. 09.01.01:91-92 and D-07 (:356) state edit-of/remaster-of/alternate-take-of inherit the parent's consented master ledger by reference; 09.01.02:35-36 attaches a ledger to exactly one rights object, :139-140 opens a fresh unallocated ledger on object creation, and 09.01.02's own cross-cut note to 09.01.01 (:236) restates the universal rule ('the object creates an `unallocated` ledger on creation') with no inheritance carve-out. grep across the whole domain shows the words inherit/lineage/edit-of/fork appear in no file other than 09.01.01, so 09.01.02 never adopted the rule. 09.01.01:329 itself states the tension is unresolved ('must be reconciled at Step 6 ... (b) is the live one — 09.01.02 D-01 says consent is to the whole ledger'). Downgraded from blocking because the product behaviour and the fork semantics ARE stated affirmatively at 09.01.01:91-95 and D-07, so an implementer following specific-over-general is not inventing behaviour from nothing; the divergence is that the ledger-owning feature restates the contradicting general rule.

Quotes verify but the reconciliation is explicit in the cited text itself. 09.02.03 DT-01 (:176) resolves to 'present in the view, structurally distinct in the record', and D-02 (:213) repeats it; 09.01.02:175 implements exactly that — the 0% row is 'shown with "0% — paid by fee, not by share", linking to the WFH designation', i.e. NOT the 'bare 0% row' DT-01 rejects. 09.02.03:115 renders the same party as 'Fee, no share — consented, £200 ... structurally distinct in the record from a 0% row nobody filled in'. Both files therefore specify identical user-visible behaviour; whether the row physically lives in the ledger table or is joined from the designation record is a persistence-model question for a later layer. 09.02.04 D-14 (:277) forbids an *amendment* producing a 0% row (the zeroing path), not the existence of a designation-linked row. 09.01.05 D-01 (:97) states disjointness as 'either, both, or neither', which permits a 0% performer row rather than forbidding it, and 09.02.03 DT-04 (:179) puts the WFH party's consent on the designation (designee + payer), so ledger 'Waiting on N of M' arithmetic is unaffected either way.

All quotes verify verbatim and directly contradict with no marker on either side. 09.01.04:162 'Save blocked' and :197 'save disabled' for a publisher pool that does not reconcile to its anchor writer's share; 09.01.02 D-05 (:262) 'Save is never gated; Propose is', :167 'Save is never blocked; the Propose button carries the reason', and DT-10 (:229) explicitly REJECTS blocked-save as 'a data-loss path aimed precisely at the persona whose lazy path must be the correct path'. 09.01.04:22-24 concedes 09.01.02 is the validator and that it contributes only the anchoring invariant to it, and 09.02.04:80 treats D-05 as governing ('Draft | Saved always, never gated ([09.01.02] D-05)'). Two implementers build opposite persistence behaviour for the same mid-session draft, and one of them loses capture data the domain's thesis says is unrepeatable.

Quotes verify (09.01.02:49 INV-2 'checked separately and reported separately'; 09.01.04:53 and D-05 :250 'never an independent check'), but the two rules accept and reject exactly the same set of ledgers. Given INV-3 / 09.01.04 rule 2 (per-writer anchoring, 09.01.02:50) plus the writer-pool-100% check, a publisher pool total other than 100% is unreachable while every anchor matches — so the publisher-pool sum is genuinely derived and adds no accept/reject decision. The 150/50 example at 09.01.02:169 is caught by INV-2's writer-pool clause regardless. What differs is only which remainder string is rendered ('Publisher shares total 50%' vs the per-writer remainder at 09.01.04:162), i.e. error copy for a defect both readings reject. No implementer ships a ledger the other would refuse.

The quoted line scopes itself out of the conflict. 09.01.02:183 reads 'Field-level last-write-wins **within `unallocated` only** — nobody has consented, so there is nothing to protect', i.e. pre-proposal drafting, and the same row still routes the draft through Propose. CX-01 s5 (09.01-rights-registry-cx.md:42) governs the binding act — 'Ledger writes must be proposals requiring consent' — which 09.01.02 satisfies at :184 (two Proposes never merge, second rejected as stale) and :185 (consent against a changed version rejected as stale). Both sibling citations are post-draft contexts: 09.01.04:184 is a transfer racing an amendment on a consented anchor, and 09.01.01 D-12 (:361) is a *link* write, not a draft ledger field. No reading has an unconsented draft edit bind anyone.

The exception is stated explicitly in the same file that states the rule, in the table where exceptions belong. 09.01.03:203 (Happy Path, recording created with a work) says both ledgers open; 09.01.03:251 (Edge Cases) carves out 'Master with no linked work ... No phantom publishing ledger is created, and no "incomplete" warning is shown for its absence', and 09.01.02:193 agrees ('has a master ledger and no publishing ledger yet'). 09.01.01:248 shows the publishing layer arriving with the work, not the recording. The finding's stated forced invention — whether the pair-incomplete indicator fires for an unlinked recording — is answered twice: 09.01.02:214 defines Pair-incomplete as 'One of a work/recording ledger **pair**', so no pair exists, and 09.01.03:251 says no warning is shown.

Quotes verify, but what is missing is a field list, not a behaviour. 09.01.01:69 is a one-line summary of the link ('a type and a weight'), not a schema; :105-107 and :270-271 specify the product behaviour completely — declared disjoint spans get duration proration as an editable proposal ('each work's share of the recording's running time'), declared temporal overlap gets no automatic allocation and requires declarant-entered exact rationals, and :271/:304 give the copy for both. Disjointness is 'declared' by the declarant in both citations, so no disjointness test is owed. That proration presupposes span data is derivable from the specified behaviour; adding start/end to the link is exactly the entity-field work the architecture layer owns. Two implementers build the same two branches with the same user-visible outcomes.

Both targets are past — rights-ownership-cx.md:5 records '[DEEP] ... all sub-domain pairs synthesised from **Step-6** feature-level evidence' (dated 2026-07-23), 09.01.03:335 marks Q-08 RESOLVED by 'Step 6 CX synthesis', and 09.02.02:106-107 marks Q-02/Q-03 '✅ Resolved Step 5'. Quotes verify but the three-verdict set forces a single answer. 09.01.03:157 names the blocker AND its evaluation semantics in the same cell ('a recorded moral-rights assertion — surfaced, never evaluated for integrity'), so the block fires on the existence of a recorded assertion and the platform never judges derogatory treatment. The alternatives are unavailable: :133 'No recorded obstacle' is false once an assertion is recorded, and :134 'Unknown — terms not recorded' applies only when 'the relevant term is absent, or its source is unreachable', which is not this case. :159 further makes every block overridable by an attested owner, so nothing is permanently barred. Both implementers render Blocked-by naming the assertion and its holder.

Quotes verify, but each cadence is stated by the feature that owns its own flow, so nothing is left to invent. 09.02.01:106-118 heads its table 'The consent chase — concretely / This feature's requirement on the Consent Chase & Escalating Notification cross-cut' — capture's chase. 09.02.04:172/:221 states the amendment-proposal cadence (day 0/7/21, badge `blocked` at day 45) inside the amendment lifecycle, and preserves the same governing invariants (':172 The proposal never expires and silence is never converted into consent'). rights-ownership-cx.md:289 records capture's numbers as the domain's requirement on a shared notification mechanism, which is a component parameterisation question, not a behavioural fork. No user-visible outcome is undetermined.

Quotes verify and the contradiction is normative on both sides with no marker. 09.01.01:289 and :334 make `public-domain` a terminal publishing-ledger state that 'satisfies the release gate', and :342 confirms '`public-domain` does not' resolve to a release refusal. 09.03.05 D-06 (:119) says a determinate term status 'is not clearance, legal advice, ownership, or release authorization' and :80 'Licensing and release retain their independent evidence/permission gates'; :52-54 repeats 'not ... a release-gate override'. The write path is also absent: 09.03.05's States table (:83-91) emits per-territory statuses only, never a ledger state, and D-03 (:116) makes term 'computed, never declared — read-only to all personas', while 09.01.01:289 says 'The determination is [09.03.05]'s, never this feature's'. A repo-wide grep shows no other file mentions the state. Territory compounds it: 09.03.05 determines only US/FR/DE/GB with everything else `unknown`, while 09.01.02 D-15/:198 gives the ledger exactly one territory (`World`), and no mapping rule exists anywhere. An implementer must invent both the writer of the state and the jurisdiction collapse.

Both open questions are well-formed [OWNER] deferrals with an owner and a live target, and neither is blind to the in-domain material. 09.04-rights-conflicts-disputes-index.md:61 Q-02 carries 'Owner: User | Deferred To: `/create-prd`' and itself records the existing partial constraint ('domain 12 already blocks a *pre-delivery* release on contested ownership ([12.01.01 D-07]), but the live-release half is the same open owner call there'); 09.04.03:112 Q-04 does the same. They also address a different object from the cited 'settled' text: 09.01.03's Control Summary is an advisory derived verdict surface whose blocks are all overridable by an attested owner (09.01.03:159, D-06 :316) and whose enforcement 09.01.01 D-08 (:357) hands entirely to domain 12. Rendering `disputed` as a Blocked-by verdict and actually refusing a live release or a licence are separate calls, and only the second is deferred.

Quotes verify verbatim on both sides, with no marker on either. 09.04-rights-conflicts-disputes-cx.md:85 R-03 states the objection 'routes to [domain 24] **directly**' and that 'Handling it here would drag an integrity judgement into a machine built for arithmetic'. 09.03.06:23 (Role Lens) and :72 (Edge Cases) both state it 'routes to [09.04] and [domain 24]'. How a non-resolving dispute ends is a live [OWNER] deferral with owner and target — 09.04.02:57 '`[PENDING — resolution of Q-01 at /create-prd]`' and 09.04-rights-conflicts-disputes-index.md:60 Q-01 (User, `/create-prd`). What is left unstated is the countdown's numeric value, a tuning parameter that changes no rights outcome.

Both required; missing NIL blocks (CX-02)') supply the knowable triggers. Verified by direct comparison against disk. rights-ownership-index.md:28 asserts 'All nodes `[SURFACE]`; the domain is `[BREADTH]`' and the Children table (:32-37) carries `[SURFACE]` for all six sub-domains. Every sub-domain index on disk declares '> **Status**: [BREADTH]' (09.01–09.06), the domain CX declares [DEEP], and the 26 leaves split [DEEP] ×8 (09.01.01-.04, 09.02.01, 09.02.03, 09.02.04, plus none other), [PARTIAL] ×12 and [SURFACE] ×6.
